job.title: Business Insights Analyst
job.description:
The Opportunity
This permanent Christchurch-based role is for a Data & BI Analyst who will support finance and accounting processes through data analysis, reporting and system support. The position involves eliciting and documenting business requirements, analysing current processes, developing Power BI reports and SQL queries, and supporting operational applications and ERP systems used for accounting and financial data. Work includes partnering with stakeholders on reporting needs, maintaining data integrity across finance and operational outputs, assisting with system testing, UAT, configuration and post-implementation support, and contributing to project and change activities.

The Company
The organisation is an established New Zealand business operating from Christchurch. It maintains core enterprise systems including ERP platforms used for accounting and finance, alongside reporting and data tools. The role sits within a team that supports internal users across operational and financial processes.

The Role
  • Elicit, document and validate business requirements for reporting and system changes, with emphasis on finance and accounting data.
  • Analyse current-state processes and identify improvement opportunities in data flows, reporting and operational applications.
  • Develop and maintain Power BI dashboards, semantic models, DAX measures and reports aligned to operational and financial KPIs.
  • Write and optimise SQL queries for data extraction, transformation, validation, reconciliation and analysis.
  • Support implementation, configuration, testing, UAT and deployment of operational applications and ERP accounting systems.
  • Review and improve data pipelines, Lakehouse/Warehouse structures and models; investigate and resolve data quality, refresh and reporting issues.
  • Maintain documentation, configuration records, reporting schedules and registers.
  • Contribute to project planning, tracking, change management, training materials and user communications.
  • Act as liaison between IT and operational/finance teams; provide guidance, troubleshooting and updates to stakeholders.
  • Support administrative tasks related to systems, data and internal/supplier queries.
  • Comply with safety policies and contribute to a safety-first culture.
Your Profile
  • Ability to translate business requirements into practical reporting and system support solutions.
  • Experience in data analysis, Business Intelligence or analytics delivery, preferably involving finance or accounting data.
  • Power BI development experience, including semantic modelling and DAX.
  • SQL skills for querying, transforming, validating and reconciling data.
  • Exposure to ERP systems used for accounting and related data integration.
  • Communication and stakeholder engagement skills suitable for working with finance, operations and IT users.
  • Valid working rights for New Zealand.

job.title: Head of Commercial - Merchandise
job.description:
The Opportunity
You’ll step into a role where the commercial frameworks are already in place and the next job is to build a high-performance culture. It is a leadership seat on the Merchandise Leadership Team, reporting to the GM Merchandise, where you partner with Heads of Business, influence trading decisions, and hold the commercial discipline that keeps supplier value and member benefit front of mind.

The team of commercial analysts are professional, self-sufficient and mostly made up of chartered accountants. You will lead them, resource them, and give them the strategic air cover so they can keep delivering the fact base the trading teams rely on. Your own time will go to the forward-looking work: annual trade budgeting, commercial governance, and the conversations that decide where the next sale, unit and dollar of profit comes from.

It is a high-performance environment. You will be expected to challenge constructively, stay comfortable with the trade-offs between pure analysis and commercial judgement, and bring the temperament to operate at pace without losing the relationships that make the work possible.

The Company
Foodstuffs South Island is the co-operative that feeds the South Island and works to create successful communities. It is one of the region’s largest employers, owned by its members and present in nearly every community across the island.

The Merchandise division sits at the centre of that. It negotiates with suppliers, manages the commercial terms that apply at product and supplier level, and partners with trading teams so the right product arrives for the right customer at the right cost. You will work alongside Retail, Supply Chain, Finance and the wider Merchandise leadership group.

The purpose is straightforward: better commercial outcomes that ultimately benefit members, customers and the communities the co-operative serves.

The Role
Your week will include:
  • Lead the commercial performance of the Merchandise function, identifying opportunities to maximise profitability, supplier value and member benefit.
  • Drive the annual trade budgeting process with Finance, Retail and the Heads of Business, then cascade and review it through the year.
  • Oversee supplier commercial agreements, trading terms and rebate programmes so activity matches expected commercial outcomes.
  • Partner with Merchandise, Retail, Supply Chain and Finance teams to surface, prioritise and deliver commercial opportunities.
  • Provide timely, accurate commercial insight that supports both operational decisions and longer-term strategy.
  • Lead and develop a high-performing commercial team, including performance, capability and succession.
  • Monitor commercial performance against budget and forecast, and lead the analysis and business cases that improve returns.
Your Profile
You will bring:
  • Significant leadership experience in a senior commercial, category, supplier management or business leadership role, typically 10–15+ years of relevant depth.
  • Proven ability to drive commercial performance and deliver financial outcomes in a complex, multi-stakeholder environment.
  • Strong commercial acumen, including experience managing supplier relationships, commercial negotiations and value-creation work.
  • The ability to influence senior stakeholders and contribute effectively as a member of a leadership team.
  • Experience developing and leading high-performing teams, preferably with analytical or accounting specialists.
  • Strong financial literacy and the capacity to move quickly from a high-level view to the detail that shows where money is made or lost.
  • Comfort operating in a high-performance culture: constructive challenge, clear expectations, and the temperament for pace and trade-offs.
Experience in FMCG, grocery retail, wholesale or distribution is an advantage, as is a CA qualification, but neither is a hard requirement. What matters is that you are commercially wired and forward-looking.

Full working rights are required, and no sponsorship is offered.

A privately held New Zealand business is seeking an experienced senior finance professional for a fixed-term assignment through to end of winter 2027.

Working alongside the existing finance lead and business owners, you will strengthen cashflow visibility, improve financial reporting and establish more efficient finance processes across a multi-entity environment. A major focus will be developing robust financial models and introducing practical, well-controlled uses of AI within the finance function.

This is a hands-on position rather than a purely advisory engagement. You will initially take ownership of the more technically complex work, before progressively transferring knowledge and responsibility to the internal finance team.

This established private business operates through multiple entities and projects. It is entering a period of finance improvement, with an emphasis on clearer information, stronger systems and developing its internal capability.

The environment is commercially focused, collaborative and relatively informal. Due to the confidential nature of the appointment, further information will be provided during the recruitment process.

The Role
  • Review existing finance processes, systems, reporting and information flows.
  • Establish reliable consolidated cashflow forecasting across multiple entities and projects.
  • Build and maintain cashflow, funding and reforecasting models with clearly linked assumptions and schedules.
  • Improve monthly reporting for business owners and external stakeholders.
  • Streamline month-end, payment, reconciliation and management reporting processes.
  • Introduce practical AI-enabled workflows across reporting, analysis and financial review.
  • Assess the value of existing finance tools and recommend whether they should be retained or replaced.
  • Document processes, models and AI workflows to support consistent future use.
  • Mentor the internal finance lead in financial modelling, forecasting and AI-enabled finance processes.
  • Complete a structured handover so the improved finance function can operate independently.

Your Profile
  • A senior finance background gained as a Finance Manager, Financial Controller, CFO or experienced finance consultant.
  • CA, CPA, CIMA qualification or equivalent experience would be advantageous.
  • Advanced financial modelling and cashflow forecasting capability using Excel.
  • Experience working across multi-entity, project-based or similarly complex organisations.
  • Practical experience applying generative AI tools within finance processes.
  • Strong understanding of New Zealand financial reporting, GST and tax requirements.
  • Experience producing clear financial information for business owners, directors, funders or lenders.
  • A hands-on approach and the ability to move comfortably between strategic priorities and detailed implementation.
  • A collaborative mentoring style, with the patience to build capability rather than retain knowledge.

The Opportunity
This is Evnex’s first dedicated Finance Business Partner role. The finance team has built the foundations: actuals reported as an integrated three-statement set, a 13-week cash flow forecast, and a new 12-month rolling forecast model being implemented now. Your job is to pick that work up, own it in detail, and take it to the next level.
  
You will report to the senior finance manager and work closely with the CFO on the forecast model, the annual budget, and the quarterly board pack. You will also partner with leaders across the business, turning financial analysis into decisions and following through on the actions agreed. The finance function is striving for global best practice for a business of its size, and AI tools are part of how the work gets done every day.
  
This is a step-up role for someone who has already done the work and now wants ownership of it. In your first two weeks you will build your own 90-day plan, and there is a clear path to grow as Evnex and its finance team scale.
  
The Company
Founded in Christchurch, Evnex designs and manufactures smart EV chargers for homes and businesses across New Zealand and Australia, including the Evnex E2 range and the X-series. More than 20,000 Evnex chargers are now installed across the two countries. Its mission is to make electrification effortless, and the clean energy transition is the reason the company exists.
  
Evnex is a Series A, private equity backed company. The business is growing, holds significant inventory, and reports quarterly to its board and investors. It is a small team solving a hard problem, where most people do more than their title suggests and everyone is expected to own their work.
  
The Role
  • Take ownership of the new forecast model and run it as an integrated three-statement, 12-month rolling forecast, working closely with the CFO on its development and build-out
  • Run the annual budget with the CFO, and the monthly to quarterly reforecast and variance analysis, with commentary for the leadership team
  • Work alongside the CFO in preparing the quarterly board pack
  • Run the weekly 13-week cash flow forecast cycle and variance analysis with the senior finance manager
  • Partner with department leads on detailed financial analysis that drives business improvement
  • Improve models and data flows from Business Central and HubSpot, using AI and automation to reduce manual work
  • Support the senior finance manager with month-end analysis, a small and capped part of the role
  
Your Profile
  • CA or CPA qualified, or close to it, with at least three years’ finance experience
  • Hands-on experience doing forecasting, budgeting, and variance analysis yourself, not only reviewing it
  • A working understanding of how the P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow statement link

  • Experience in a manufacturing, distribution, or inventory-intensive business is desirable but not essential

job.title: Commercial Accountant
job.description:
Louis-pbentley The Opportunity
This is a broad commercial seat, not a narrow ledger role. A Christchurch expe business needs someone who can sit with operations, build the numbers behind each project, and still roll their sleeves up when the finance team is short.
You will model pricing across programmes, build detailed budgets with the operational staff who used to own that work, and look at margins with the people who can actually change them. Alongside that sits a live systems project: due diligence and support on a new ERP, plus room to use AI where it makes dashboards and analysis faster.

Month-end is shared, not owned end to end. You will help the team hit a working-day-ten close, support wash-ups, and step in on year-end IFRS reporting when it is needed. The rest of the week is commercial: fees, surcharges, stakeholder questions, and the odd transactional job that keeps the Financial Accountant and Management Accountant moving.
If you like a mixed bag, and you would rather improve a process than protect one, this is that role. The business name stays confidential until you are ready to talk.

The Company
A small team with global footprint. You will work with operational staff, the Financial Accountant and the Management Accountant. Personality matters here. The useful version of this role is curious, plain-spoken, and comfortable switching between a pricing model and a cutoff.
The Role A usual stretch of work looks like this:
  • Model pricing for programmes and test how changes land on yield and margin.
  • Build detailed budgets with operational staff, as that work moves into accounts.
  • Partner on margin analysis, and work through payment fees and surcharge settings with the right stakeholders.
  • Support due diligence and implementation of a new ERP, including how trip, commercial and finance data should connect.
  • Help the team hit the working-day-ten close, including wash-ups and occasional month-end support.
  • Support year-end IFRS reporting, and pick up transactional work for the Financial Accountant and Management Accountant.
  • Use AI and modern tools to build dashboards and shorten analysis the team currently does by hand.
  • Various more transactional work to support the wider team when required
Your Profile
You will bring:
  • A background in management or commercial accounting, with real time in budgeting, pricing or margin work. A degree or progress towards CA is useful, not a gate.
  • Comfort with systems. You can hold your own in an ERP review, and you like fixing how data moves, not only how a spreadsheet looks.
  • A digital habit. You already use AI, or you are keen to, for dashboards, analysis and the repetitive parts of finance.
  • Sound interpersonal skills. Operations will only hand over budgets if they trust the person asking the questions.
  • An analytical eye and a practical streak. You can support a close on working day ten and still come back to the commercial question afterwards.
How to Apply

If this sounds like the next step you have been looking for, we would like to hear from you. Apply via the relevant link or reach out for a confidential conversation: Louis | louis@profilegroup.co.nz | 0224 269 569.
